title: Security Firewall for Agents — Ryan Dahl, Deno
talk_summary: Ryan Dahl describes running incident-response agents with broad read/write access to Postgres, Kubernetes, ClickHouse, AWS, GitHub and Slack, and argues the agent itself must be treated as untrusted software. He presents Claw Patrol, an MIT-licensed byte-level egress proxy that parses protocols (including non-HTTP like Postgres), injects credentials, and enforces HCL rules with deny/LLM-judge/human-approval actions.

takeaways.technique: Egress proxy as the security boundary, not in-agent guards
takeaways.what_they_do: All agent network traffic is forced through a proxy that parses each protocol and applies rules; the agent software is a black box and needs no modification.
takeaways.evidence_quote: the agents themselves have to be untrusted software. You can't rely on the agent itself to guard what it's doing.

takeaways.technique: Credential injection so agents never see secrets
takeaways.what_they_do: The proxy holds real credentials and substitutes placeholders in outbound requests, so agent processes and their context never contain secret values.
takeaways.evidence_quote: the agent itself never actually sees the credentials of the system that it's talking to but passes some placeholder out and the proxy itself injects those credentials

takeaways.technique: Versioned, tested policy file with fixture unit tests
takeaways.what_they_do: Permissions live in a ~1000-line HCL file checked into git, with a test harness where fixture requests must be blocked by the rule set.
takeaways.evidence_quote: this rule file actually has a test system along with it where you can provide uh fixtures action like fixture requests that can flow through the rules

takeaways.technique: Tiered actions: deny / LLM-judge / human approval
takeaways.what_they_do: Rules can reject outright, escalate to an LLM judge, or request human approval in Slack, and can chain them (judge then human).
takeaways.evidence_quote: you can define rules that don't just reject requests or actions but uh ask a human for example in a slack channel or run an LLM judge

takeaways.what_they_do: The proxy understands Postgres and other non-HTTP protocols and can block specific functions even when traffic tunnels through other systems.
takeaways.evidence_quote: Postgress being a nonHTP protocol and these rules can be applied even when tunneling through other systems

takeaways.technique: Standalone VM isolation plus network-only control surface
takeaways.what_they_do: Agents run on isolated VMs so filesystem/syscall sandboxing is unnecessary; all meaningful actions reduce to network bytes, which the proxy governs.
takeaways.evidence_quote: we provision uh standalone VM for for our agents
